subject: BIOL
title: RNA Processing
desc: An advanced graduate-level course on biological aspects of RNA function and processing in eukaryotes. Lectures and discussions will be developed using the current literature.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 200B or permission of instructor. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Ribosomes and Translation
desc: Covers the field of ribosome research in depth, including the structure and function of ribosomes and the molecular mechanisms of protein synthesis. Begins with historical review of the ribosome field and proceeds to the most recent findings. Focus is on central questions: (1) How is the accuracy of the aminoacyl-tRNA selection determined? (2) What is accommodation? (3) What is the mechanism of peptide bond formation (peptidyl transferase)? (4) What is the mechanism of translocation? (5) What are the mechanistic roles of the ribosome and translation factor EF-G in translocation? (6) To what extent is the mechanism of translation determined by RNA? (7) Why is RNA so well suited for the ribosome? (8) How did translation evolve from an RNA world?
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOC 100A, BIOL 200B or permission of instructor. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Chromatin
desc: Eukaryotic DNA is complexed with histones to form chromatin. This course focuses on the ways in which chromatin influences and is manipulated to regulate gene expression
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 105 and BIOL 115; undergrads by permission of instructor. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Epigenetics
desc: In-depth coverage of epigenetics focusing on how alterations in chromatin structure and DNA methylation establish and maintain heritable states of gene expression. Lectures are supplemented with critical discussion of recent publications.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 105 and BIOL 115, or permission of instructor. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Stem Cell Biology
desc: Fundamental concepts, experimental approaches, and current advances in stem cell biology, with consideration of key ethical issues. Topics include: self-renewal and differentiation; the microenvironment; epigenetics; cell-cycle regulation; and how basic research translates to medical therapeutics. Ethical, moral, and political issues surrounding stem cell research are discussed with lectures from philosophy and other relevant disciplines.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Current Protocols in Stem Cell Biology
desc: Provides students with hands-on experience in embryonic stem cell culture methods.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll by permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Cellular Signaling Mechanisms
desc: All eukaryotic cells utilize intricate signaling pathways to control such diverse events as cell-cell communication, cell division, and changes in cell morphology. This course covers the molecular basis of these cellular signaling pathways, focusing on the most current research.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 105, BIOL 110, and BIOL 115. Enrollment is restricted to seniors and graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Cell and Molecular Biology
desc: Introduction to biochemistry, cell biology, molecular biology, and genetics.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): CHEM 1A, CHEM 3A, or CHEM 4A. First pass enrollment restricted to proposed majors in the following: Biology BA, Biology BS, MCD Biology BS, Neuroscience BS, Ecology and Evolutionary Biology BS, Marine Biology BS, Plant Sciences BS, EEB/ENVS combined BA, Global and Community Health BS, Biochemistry and Molecular Biology BS, Microbiology BS, Science Education BS, Biomolecular Engineering BS, or Biotechnology BA.

subject: BIOL
title: Experimental Biology Laboratory
desc: Provides biology majors with the theory and practice of experimental biology. A wide range of concepts and techniques used in the modern laboratory are included in the exercises. Designed to satisfy the introductory biology lab requirement of many medical and professional schools.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 20A and previous or concurrent enrollment in BIOE 20B.

subject: BIOL
title: Genetics Preparatory Course
desc: Prepares students for BIOL 105, Introduction to Genetics. Core concepts in Mendelian and molecular genetics aree covered. These include mitosis, meiosis, the chromosome theory of inheritance, complementation, pedigree analysis, replication, and fundamental concepts in molecular biology.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 20A.

subject: BIOL
title: Advances in Cancer Biology
desc: Provides students with knowledge of the latest concepts in cancer biology and cancer therapeutics, and a general appreciation of the rapid advances being made in this area of biomedicine.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 200B or by permission of instructor. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Applied Statistics for Molecular, Cell, and Developmental Biology
desc: For experimental biologists: focuses on resolving practical statistical issues typically encountered in molecular, cellular, and developmental biology lab research. No prior experience in statistics or programming is necessary.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students in molecular, cellular, and developmental biology.

subject: BIOL
title: Influence of Environment and Experience on Brain Development
desc: How environmental factors (animals' experiences, environmental toxins, etc.) affect the formation of neuronal circuits and brain function. Lectures and discussions use current literature.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 200A, BIOL 200B, BIOL 200C, and BIOL 200D, or by permission of the instructor. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: CRISPR/Cas Technologies
desc: Provides an overview of the continually emerging roles for CRISPR in biomedical research. Topics will include an overview of the CRISPR genome defense systems in bacteria, the mechanisms of DNA cleavage and repair, the many uses of CRISPR as a genome editing tool in model organisms, and discussions on the ethical use of the technology in precision medicine.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 200A, BIOL 200B, and BIOL 200C. Enrollment restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: STEM Outreach
desc: Trains students how to plan, design, and develop STEM outreach programs. Outreach proposals focused on engaging communities from under-represented backgrounds.

subject: BIOL
title: Intro to Science Communication: Public Speaking and Science Writing
desc: Course centers around developing practical skills for communicating science across various formats and to different audiences. Through guest lectures, peer feedback and presentations, students learn how to craft a short talk for the general public, short science videos, and write accessible opinion editorials for the public. Students gain experience adapting their communication style for various audiences and build confidence in science speaking and writing.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Neural Plasticity and Cognitive Neuroscience
desc: Focuses on the dynamic aspect of the nervous system and how it subserves various cognitive functions. Course examines formation and plasticity of synapses, the fundamental units of neural circuits. Course also explores the neural circuit mechanisms that underlie various cognitive functions, and how they go astray in neurological disorders. In addition to textbook materials, students learn to read review articles and classic original research papers on pertinent topics, and write topic specific reviews. Students cannot receive credit for this course and BIOL 126. (Formerly Advanced Molecular Neuroscience.)
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Studying Brain Development: From Stem Cells to Neural Circuits
desc: Covers the current research efforts and up-to-date methods in the fields of stem cells and developmental neuroscience. Students learn the principles controlling stem cell differentiation, brain development, circuit formation, and plasticity. The topics include neural stem cell lineage analysis, neurogenesis, cell fate specification, neural circuit formation and mapping, brain activity and circuit formation, and how circuits are modified by experience. This course is intended for graduate students working in the fields of stem cell biology and neural development and those interested in neuroscience as a potential research career.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students. Undergraduates may enroll with permission.

subject: BIOL
title: Developmental Neurobiology
desc: Covers the principles of nervous-system development from the molecular control of development, and cell-cell interactions, to the role of experience in influencing brain structure and function. Students cannot receive credit for this course and course 128. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students and by permission of the instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Grant Writing in the Biomedical Sciences
desc: Introduction to the fundamentals of grant writing in biomedical research, including best practices for presentation of data and communication of research findings. Participants write and peer-edit most components of the NIH Ruth Kirschstein F31/F32 pre- or post-doctoral fellowship.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Stem Cell Research: Scientific, Ethical, Social, and Legal Issues
desc: Investigates the scientific, ethical, social, and legal dimensions of human embryonic stem-cell research, including the moral status of the embryo; the concept of respect for life; ethical constraints on oocyte procurement; creation of embryonic chimeras; federal policies; and political realities. (Also offered as Biomolecular Engineering 247. Students cannot receive credit for both courses.) Prerequisite(s): Course in stem cell biology (ex: BME 278 Stem Cell Research) or the equivalent knowledge. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): Course in stem cell biology (ex: BME 278 Stem Cell Research) or the equivalent knowledge. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Frosh/Soph Seminar in Neuroscience
desc: Overview of the field of neuroscience for students considering the neuroscience major or related academic programs. Talks by neuroscience faculty on research on nervous system function, approaches to understanding behavior, and neurological disorders/disease. Also, overview of neuroscience careers and UC Santa Cruz’s neuroscience major.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to freshman and sophomore proposed majors in biochemistry and molecular biology, biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics, cognitive science, ecology and evolution, global and community health (B.S.), marine biology, microbiology, molecular cell and developmental biology, neuroscience, biology B.A, biology B.S., biotechnology, and psychology.

subject: BIOL
title: Frosh/Soph Seminar in Molecular & Cell Biology
desc: Overview of molecular and cell biology for students considering MCD biology and related majors. Talks by MCDB faculty on their labs’ biomedical research programs and by scientists and clinicians on careers in the field. Overview of MCDB majors.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to first-year and sophomore proposed majors in biochemistry and molecular biology, biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics, cognitive science, ecology and evolution, global and community health (B.S.), marine biology, microbiology, molecular cell and developmental biology, neuroscience, biology B.A, biology B.S., biotechnology.

subject: BIOL
title: Topics in Research on Molecular Genetics of Yeast
desc: Intensive research seminar on the structure and function of the gene expression machinery in the simple eukaryote Saccharomyces cervisiae and its relationship to the human gene expression machinery.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with approval of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Chromatin Structure and Transcriptional Regulation
desc: Weekly seminar on structure and gene regulatory function of chromatin. Discusses research of participants and relevant scientific literature.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Mammalian Brain Development
desc: Seminar covers research into the development of the mammalian brain.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Muscle Biology and Gene Regulation
desc: Weekly seminar and group discussion on current topics in the study of muscle biology and gene regulation as it relates to transcriptional dynamics. Students present, review, and discuss relevant research pertaining but not limited to muscle development, epigenetics, and skeletal muscle adaptation. In addition to presenting and discussing published research, students present their own independent research and receive feedback from the instructor and other students.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to molecular, cell, and developmental biology graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Meiotic Chromosome Dynamics
desc: Intensive course on the molecular mechanisms underlying homolog pairing, synapses, and recombination; and how they are regulated, coordinated, and monitored to ensure accurate meiotic chromosome segregation.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Development of Vertebrate Neural Connections
desc: Intensive research seminar on molecular mechanisms by which neural connections are established during mouse development. Special focus on topographic maps and role of Eph receptors and ephrins in this process.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Mechanisms of Behavioral Development and Evolution
desc: Weekly seminar and group discussion on current topics in the study of birdsong neurobiology and the development and evolution of the nervous system generally. Students present, review, and discuss relevant research pertaining but not limited to birdsong molecular and systems neurobiology, developmental gene regulatory mechanisms in the brain, and comparative neurobiology. In addition to presenting and discussing published research, students present their own independent research and receive feedback from the instructor and other students.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Topics on Research into Chromatin and Transcription
desc: Seminar covering research into the effects of chromatin on transcription in yeast.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Epigenetic Gene Silencing and Insulators
desc: Intensive course on molecular mechanisms by which insulator elements regulate epigenetic gene silencing.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Structures of Macromolecular Complexes
desc: Focuses on structure and function of the spliceosome using electron microscopy and x-ray crystallography. Participants present results from their own research and relevant journal articles.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Topics in Cell Cycle Research
desc: An intensive seminar focusing on current research on the molecular mechanisms that control cell division. Participants are required to present results of their own research or to review journal articles of interest.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Development
desc: Seminar covering research into breast development and cancer.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Post-Transcriptional Control of Mammalian Gene Expression
desc: Intensive course on the molecular mechanisms by which RNA binding proteins regulate gene expression.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with the permission of the instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Long Noncoding RNA and the Immune System
desc: Weekly seminar discussion of the current research and literature concerning the functions for long noncoding RNA in gene regulation within inflammatory signaling pathways.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll by permission of the instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Translation Regulation by RNA structure
desc: Weekly seminar and group discussion on current topics in the study of RNA structures that influence translation in eukaryotic systems. Students present, review, and discuss relevant research pertaining but not limited to RNA structure-function relationships, mechanisms underlying alternative or non-canonical modes of translation initiation, methods of macromolecular structure determination, recapitulation of eukaryotic translation in cell-free systems, and computational homology-based search methods for widespread viral RNA structures. In addition to presenting and discussing published research, students present their own independent research and receive feedback.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to molecular, cell, and developmental biology graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Quality Control in Gene Expression
desc: Intensive, discussion-based course concerning ongoing research in quality control and gene expression via analysis of published and unpublished observations and theories.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Telomeres and Telomerase
desc: Weekly seminar and group discussion on current topics telomerase and telomere length regulation. Students present, review, and discuss relevant research on telomerase, regulation of telomere length equilibrium, analysis of telomere length data. In addition to presenting and discussing published research, students present their own independent research and receive feedback from the instructor and other members of the laboratory. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Gene regulation in C. elegans and human parasitic namtodes
desc: Intense weekly seminar on the mechanisms of gene regulation, focusing on C. elegans and human parasitic nematodes.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with the permission of the instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Stem Cell Genomics and Neurodevelopment
desc: Weekly seminar and group discussion on current topics related to the role of human genome variants, including retrotransposons and segmental duplications, on gene regulation and human brain development and disease. Students present, review, and discuss research pertaining, but not limited, to the evolution of retrotransposons and KZNF proteins and their effect on early embryonic gene regulatory programs as well as the development and characterization of pluripotent stem cell-derived brain organoid models. In addition to presenting and discussing published research, students also present their own independent research and receive feedback from the instructor and other class participants.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Cancer Stem Cell Biology
desc: Intensive, discussion-based course covering recent published and unpublished research in mechanisms regulating cancer stem cells and metastasis in breast cancer and their relationship with normal stem cells. Students also present their own research and solicit feedback from students and instructors. May be repeated for credit. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Discussions on the Development of the Drosophila Embryo
desc: Involves a two-hour weekly meeting in which the students discuss topics concerning the cell cycle, early embryonic development, and the cytoskeleton. These discussions critically evaluate ongoing research in this area. Material is drawn from student research and recently published journal articles. Students are also expected to meet individually with the instructor two hours weekly. In addition to a three–five page research proposal, each student gives two one-hour oral presentations.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Translational pediatric genomics
desc: Weekly discussion of the current research and literature on translational pediatric genomics. Specific patient cases may be discussed.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll by permission of the instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Development, Connectivity, and Genetic Identity of Neural Circuits
desc: This seminar course will cover the current topics and progress of neuroscience research on neural circuit development, connectivity, function and genetics. (Formerly Membrane Proteins.)
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: RNA-mediated epigenetic inheritance
desc: Intensive research seminar about epigenetic inheritance and the role of small non-coding RNAs in the intergenerational inheritance of paternal environmental effects. Participants present their research results and report on related journal articles.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll by permission of the instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Activity-Dependent Synaptic Plasticity
desc: Research seminar covering the regulation of synaptic plasticity in the mammalian nervous system, focusing on how the activity regulates the structural and functional dynamics of synapses.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Prostate Development and Cancer Biology
desc: Weekly research seminar covering gene regulation, cellular interactions, and stem cell behaviors in mammalian prostate development and prostate cancer progression.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; undergraduates may enroll by the permission of the instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Host Responses to Respiratory Viral Infections
desc: Weekly seminar and discussion of current research and literature concerning mechanisms by which the host immune response determines the severity of disease following a respiratory viral infection. Enrollment is limited to 10.
prereq_raw: Enrollment restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Mucosal Immunology and Microbiology
desc: Weekly seminar covering current research and literature concerning the gut barrier and microbes, with particular emphasis on enteric viruses. Enrollment is limited to 10.
prereq_raw: Enrollment restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Lentiviral Replication
desc: Weekly seminar and discussion on current research and literature related to lentiviral replication, evolution, and cross-species transmission as it relates to the host DNA damage response and antiviral innate immunity. Participants present their research results, report on relevant journal articles, and actively engage in group discussions on the topics.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to molecular, cell, and developmental biology graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Pedagogy in STEM
desc: Prepares graduate students to help teach university science courses. Weekly class sessions include activities and interactive discussions of diverse modes of learning, diverse ways of teaching, peer instruction, assessment of learning, equity and inclusion, and professional ethics. Students also visit an active learning class and an active learning discussion section at UCSC, then write evaluations of the teaching strategies used in those classes. (Formerly Teaching Assistant Training.)
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Practice of Science
desc: Examination of ethical and practical scientific issues, including the collection and treatment of data, attribution of credit, plagiarism, fraud, and peer review. Career issues, including how to apply for grants and positions in industry or academia, will be discussed.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 200A or permission of instructor. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; undergraduates may enroll with permission of the instructor.

subject: BIOL
title: Career Planning
desc: An important goal of graduate programs is to train students for diverse careers. Exposes molecular cell and developmental biology graduate students to diverse career options and helps them develop individual development plans to target their graduate training to their selected career goals.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology Seminar
desc: Topics of current interest in molecular, cellular, and developmental biology are presented weekly by graduate students, faculty, and guest speakers.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: MCD Seminar
desc: Various topics by weekly guest speakers.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Laboratory Research in Molecular, Cell, and Developmental Biology
desc: Independent laboratory research in molecular, cellular, and developmental biology. Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BIOL
title: Independent Study
desc: Independent study for graduate students who have not yet settled on a research area for their thesis. Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BIOL
title: Independent Study
desc: Independent study for graduate students who have not yet settled on a research area for their thesis. Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BIOL
title: Independent Study
desc: Independent study for graduate students who have not yet settled on a research area for their thesis. Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BIOL
title: Independent Study
desc: Independent study for graduate students who have not yet settled on a research area for their thesis. Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BIOL
title: Thesis Research
desc: Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BIOL
title: Thesis Research
desc: Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BIOL
title: Thesis Research
desc: Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BIOL
title: Thesis Research
desc: Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BIOL
title: Female Physiology and Gynecology
desc: Biochemical, medical, social, and clinical aspects of the female body. Emphasis will be on biological-chemical interactions in the female organs. Topics include female anatomy, cell physiology, endocrine functions, sexuality and intimacy, sexually transmitted diseases, puberty, pregnancy, menopause, birth control, abortion, immunity, cancer.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology of Emerging and Pandemic Diseases
desc: Designed to introduce non-biology majors to the biology of viruses, the human immune system, HIV/AIDS, and emerging viral pandemics. Also explores vaccine technology and viral mediated therapies. Social, political, and economic influences of HIV and other viral pandemics discussed.

subject: BIOL
title: Nutrition
desc: Provides an in-depth overview of human nutrition, focusing on the science of nutrients, their roles in the body, and the relationship between diet and health. Topics include macronutrients, micronutrients, metabolism, digestion, and the impact of nutrition on disease prevention and overall well-being. Course also coverd food safety, food equity and sustainability. Students gain practical skills for evaluating dietary patterns, understanding nutritional needs, and applying evidence-based practices in health promotion.

subject: BIOL
title: Nutrition of Sport
desc: The classroom environment is designed to help students connect course content to their career goals and build knowledge in ways that reflect what is known about nutrition of sports. Cooperative learning and problem solving is emphasized in lectures. Course also seeks to understand complex topics by analyzing medical test results, discussing real-world dilemmas in teams, or reading scientific papers.

subject: BIOL
title: Global Seminar: Biochemistry of Sport
desc: Helps students connect course content to their career goals and builds knowledge in ways that reflect what is known about biochemistry of sports. Cooperative learning and problem solving is emphasized in lectures. Also seeks to understand complex topics by analyzing medical test results, discussing real-world dilemmas in teams, or reading scientific papers.

subject: BIOL
title: Research Deconstruction: MCD Biology
desc: Explores scientific principles and logic through research seminars in molecular, cellular, and developmental biology. Additional topics may include diseases, stem cell biology, and other medically relevant areas in biomedical research. Prerequisite(s): Mathematics 3 or equivalent (i.e., mathematics placement examination score), and satisfaction of the Entry Level Writing and Composition requirements. Enrollment is restricted to first-year, sophomore, and junior students. Enrollment is by permission of the instructor.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): Mathematics 3 or equivalent (i.e., mathematics placement examination score), and satisfaction of the Entry Level Writing and Composition requirements.

subject: BIOL
title: Studies in Medicine: Its Art, History, Science, and Philosophy
desc: An interdisciplinary, multicultural, and historical perspective of medicine focused primarily upon therapy and practice to achieve better understanding of the scope, practice, and limits or medicine.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): satisfaction of the Entry Level Writing and Composition requirements.

subject: BME
title: Introduction to Biomolecular Engineering Problem Solving
desc: Introduction to biomolecular engineering through identification of current problems and their solutions. Intended for any student interested in BME. Students critically read primary research articles, search scientific literature, and identify relevant, trustworthy sources of information. Students learn about the engineering design process and common experimental tools used in biomolecular engineering research. Major course assignments include writing assignments and a team presentation.

subject: BME
title: Molecular Biology for Biomolecular Engineers
desc: Provides an overview of the biochemistry of three types of biomolecules. Also covers how DNA is replicated and stores genetic information, how RNA is transcribed and transports genetic information, and how proteins are synthesized and perform a variety of functions. Focuses on genes and how they are regulated.
prereq_raw: Prerequisites: BIOL 20A.

subject: BME
title: Genetics in the Genomics Era
desc: Principles of genetics and genomics focusing on how sequencing technologies enable us to understand gene function, genotype to phenotype relationships, and genetic inheritance.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 20A. Enrollment is restricted to bioengineering, biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics, biotechnology, bioinformatics, and microbiology majors and proposed majors and bioinformatics minors.

subject: BME
title: Computational Biology Tools
desc: Hands-on lectures and laboratory geared to teach basic tools and skills used in computational biology (genome browsers, sequence database searching, motif analysis, multiple sequence alignment, gene finders, phylogenetics analysis, protein structure visualization, and others). Web-based tools/databases are used on student laptops. Open to all science students; no prior programming or Unix experience required.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 105, or BIOL 100, or BIOL 105, or BIOC 100A, or CHEM 103, or bioinformatics majors, or biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics majors.

subject: BME
title: Mathematics of the Mind
desc: Investigates the mind as an adaptive system, the evolutionary history of the brain, and mathematical theories of knowledge representation and learning in humans and machines. Students build Jupyter notebooks that interact with human cerebral cortex organoids to explore adaptive processes in neural circuits. Taught in conjunction with BME 218. Students cannot receive credit for this course and BME 218.
prereq_raw: Prerequisites: either MATH 19A and MATH 19B, or MATH 20A and MATH 20B; and MATH 21 or AM 10; and CSE 20, CSE 20 Testout, or BME160; or by permission of the instructor.

subject: BME
title: Extreme Environmental Virology
desc: Examines life in extreme environments with an emphasis on the viruses that live there. Integrates aspects of virology, molecular biology, and computational biology. Students investigate a high-salt, extreme environment at the Don Edwards National Wildlife Refuge, and use DNA extraction methods to find molecular evidence of the organisms that live there and describe the genetic content of viruses and the community living in those high-salt ponds.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to College Scholar Students, and or by permission of the instructor.

subject: BME
title: Long Read Sequencing
desc: Two-credit hands-on course in DNA sequencing, sequence assembly, and gene annotation. Students make use of low-diversity metagenomic samples drawn from environmental locations to follow all steps in sequence and the discovery of prokaryotic and viral life. For students who have already completed sequencing experience in BME 23L, please consult with the instructor prior to enrolling in BME 123L to determine eligibility and course availability.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 22L, and previous or concurrent enrollment in BME 122H or BME 130.

subject: BME
title: Senior Thesis Writing
desc: For bioengineering senior thesis students, guidance in preparing a draft manuscript describing their senior research project. Students also practice conference-style oral or poster presentation.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 185 or CSE 185E. Concurrent enrollment in BME 193F or BME 195F or BME 198F or CSE 193F or CSE 195F or CSE 198F or ECE 193F or ECE 195F or ECE 198F is required. Enrollment is restricted to senior biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics and bioengineering majors.

subject: BME
title: Protein Engineering
desc: For bioengineering, bioinformatics, and biology majors, focuses on engineering (i.e., changing) of proteins. Topics focus on practical aspects of protein engineering strategies that are crucial to modern biotechnology and biomedicinal applications.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 100 or BIOC 100A or CHEM 103, or by permission of instructor.

subject: BME
title: Protein Engineering Laboratory
desc: Students address a current scientific question about protein stability using structure-guided protein engineering. Specifically, Students use recombinant DNA technology to produce an engineered protein that is predicted to have enhanced stability. Students then assess its stability with differential scanning fluorimetry.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 22L; and previous or concurrent enrollment in BME 128. Enrollment is restricted to junior and senior bioengineering, biomolecular engineering, and bioinformatics majors; other majors by permission of instructor.

subject: BME
title: Project Design and Implementation in Biomolecular Engineering I
desc: First of a three-part series focused on senior design projects in biomolecular engineering. In this first part, students examine experiments that elucidated the function of biological macromolecules at the Angstrom scale, and how technologies related to those functions were invented and implemented. Guided by these examples, each student develops a senior design project concept or small business proposal and defends its utility, plausibility, and inventiveness in a written document and an oral presentation.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 22L; BIOL 100 or BIOC 100A or CHEM 103 or BME 101; and previous or concurrent enrollment in BME 185 or CSE 185E or CSE 185S. Enrollment is restricted to junior and senior bioengineering and biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics majors or by permission of the instructor.

subject: BME
title: Project Design and Implementation in Biomolecular Engineering II
desc: Second part of a three-course sequence that is the culmination of the bioengineering program for students who chose a senior design group project to fulfill their capstone requirement. Students apply knowledge and skills gained in biomolecular engineering coursework to articulate, organize, and plan a senior design group project. Student groups complete research, specification, planning, and procurement for their project. Includes technical discussions, design reviews, and formal presentations.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 129A or BME 150. Enrollment is restricted to senior bioengineering or biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics majors.

subject: BME
title: Project Design and Implementation in Biomolecular Engineering III
desc: Final part of a three-course sequence that is the culmination of the bioengineering program for students who chose a senior design group project to fulfill their capstone requirement. Students apply knowledge and skills gained in biomolecular engineering coursework to articulate, organize, and plan a senior design group project. Student groups complete research, specification, planning, and procurement for their project. Includes technical discussions, design reviews, and formal presentations.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 129B or BME 230A. Enrollment is restricted to senior bioengineering or biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics majors.

subject: BME
title: Genomes
desc: Advanced elective for biology majors, examining biology on the genome scale. Topics include genome sequencing; large scale computational and functional analysis; features specific to prokaryotic, eukaryotic, or mammalian genomes; proteomics; SNP analysis; medical genomics; and genome evolution.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 105 or BME 105 or METX 140; or permission of the instructor.

subject: BME
title: Evolutionary Genomics
desc: Covers major recent advances in evolutionary genomics. Students learn to analyze and interpret scientific writing in depth. Students also present on work covered in the class and produce one research or review paper. Students cannot receive credit for this courses and course 232.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 105 or BIOL 105 or METX 140. Enrollment is restricted to juniors and seniors.

subject: BME
title: Bioinstrumentation
desc: Introduces the fundamental aspects of bioinstrumentation that are essential for beginning-level employment in clinical, pharmaceutical, and biotechnology laboratories. The advantages and disadvantages of several instruments are discussed and demonstrated, such as thermocycler, polymerase chain reaction (PCR), next-generation DNA sequencing platforms, pyrosequencing, fabless nanofabrication, ion-sensitive measurements, microarray fabrication, and fluorescent-activated cell sorter (FACS).
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 5; or BME 51A and BME 51B; or EE 101 and EE 101L; or BIOL 100; or BIOC 100A.

subject: BME
title: Research Programming in the Life Sciences
desc: Teaches programming while exploring object-oriented design, use of high-performance data containers (dictionaries and sets), and team-based development—all with the goal of producing reliable and usable research tools. No programming experience is required, but basic computer and molecular biology understanding is assumed. Students learn programming in Python to manipulate biological data. Programming assignments comprise the majority of the assignments, and a final project using skills developed in this course is required. Lab section registration is required. BioPython and other modules are introduced for use in the final project.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 20A or BIOL 21A.

subject: BME
title: Applied Visualization and Analysis of Scientific Data
desc: Python and its Numpy, Scipy, and Matplotlib packages as well as Inkscape are used on scientific data to generate publication-quality figures. Students cannot receive credit for this course and course 263.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 160 or BME 205 or CSE 20. Prerequisites can be waived in cases where students have the required programming skills, or who have passed the CSE 20 test-out exam. See CSE 20 Testout Exam (https://undergrad.engineering.ucsc.edu/advising/policies-forms-petitions/cse/) for resources and further information. Enrollment is restricted to juniors and seniors.

subject: BME
title: Entrepreneurship in Biotechnology
desc: Focuses on contemporary issues in commercializing biotechnology and genomics, emphasizing development of teamwork and communication skills. Topics include intellectual property management, fundraising, market analysis, and technology development as related to biotechnology start-ups. Students perform real-world tasks preparing for commercialization. Taught in conjunction with BME 275.

subject: BME
title: Engineering Stem Cells
desc: For bioengineering students interested in stem cells. Class uses project-based learning to discuss basic stem cell concepts and past breakthrough approaches to identify and design solutions for technological hurdles in stem cell research.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 20A or by consent of instructor. Basic knowledge of molecular and cellular biology is required.

subject: BME
title: Engineering Stem Cell Laboratory
desc: Introduces students to laboratory techniques for growing and differentiating embryonic stem cells, genetic manipulation of stem cells and imaging of stem cells. Students learn how to culture stem cells, count cells, transfect cells, image cells and analyze morphology of stem cells. In addition, students learn how to write lab reports and present their findings. Students are billed a materials fee of $175.
prereq_raw: Prerequisites: BME 22L; and previous or concurrent enrollment in BME 177. Enrollment is restricted to biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics majors or by permission.

subject: BME
title: Stem Cell Biology
desc: Basic concepts, experimental approaches, and therapeutic potential are discussed. Students gain experience in reading the primary scientific literature.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 110 or BME 101 or BIOC 100A or BIOL 100 or CHEM 103; BIOL 115 recommended.

subject: BME
title: Scientific Principles of Life
desc: The principles of life as it exists on this planet and how they generalize. Darwinian evolution, genomes, scientific theories of life (mechanistic, thermodynamic, information theoretic). Future of life: Internet, machine learning and adaptation, artificial intelligence, genome editing, fully artificial life.

subject: BME
title: Professional Practice in Bioengineering
desc: Seminar course where students develop a research proposal and the collaborative skills needed for independent research projects. Includes professional practice development in collaboration skills, project management, proposal development, and funding.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): previous or concurrent enrollment in BME 185 or CSE 185E. Enrollment is restricted to junior and senior bioengineering, biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics, and bioinformatics majors or by permission.

subject: BME
title: Technical Writing for Biomolecular Engineers
desc: Writing by biomolecular engineers, not to general audiences, but to engineers, engineering managers, and technical writers. Exercises include job application and resume, library puzzle, graphics, laboratory protocols, document specification, progress report, survey article or research proposal, poster, and oral presentation.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BIOL 20A; satisfaction of Entry Level Writing and Composition requirements; Enrollment restricted to junior and senior bioengineering, biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics, and biotechnology majors.

subject: BME
title: Synthetic Biology--Mentored Research A
desc: This two-credit course is the first of three courses in a 12-credit collaborative research project available to students in physical sciences, and biomolecular engineering intended to satisfy the capstone requirement. Provides a multidisciplinary, collaborative research experience working on a project in synthetic biology. Working with one or more research faculty, student teams complete a substantial project. Multiple oral/written presentations are required, including a formal conference presentation. Prerequisite(s): BME 180. Enrollment is restricted to juniors and seniors. Enrollment is by instructor permission.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 180.

subject: BME
title: Synthetic Biology--Mentored Research B
desc: This five-credit course is the second of three courses in a 12-credit collaborative research project available to students in physical sciences and biomolecular engineering intended to satisfy the capstone requirement. Multiple oral/written presentations are required, including a formal conference presentation. Prerequisite(s): BME 188A. Enrollment is restricted to juniors and seniors. Enrollment is by instructor permission.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 188A.

subject: BME
title: Synthetic Biology Mentored Research C
desc: Third of three courses in a 12-credit collaborative research project available to students in physical sciences and biomolecular engineering intended to satisfy the capstone requirement. Students in this course sequence may be participating in the annual IGEM (International Genetically Engineered Machines) competition. Course includes training in specific skills relevant to the specific sub-team and overall project, including lab-specific training (pcr, DNA electrophoresis, gel documentation, standard reagent prep, lab safety, lab equipment, project specifics). Prerequisite(s): BME 188B. Enrollment is restricted to juniors and seniors. Enrollment is by instructor permission.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 188B.

subject: BME
title: Field Study
desc: Provides for individual programs of study with specific aims and academic objectives carried out under the direction of a BME faculty member and a willing sponsor at a field site, using resources not normally available on campus. Credit is based upon written and oral presentations demonstrating the achievement of the objectives of the course. Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BME
title: Field Study
desc: Provides for individual programs of study with specific aims and academic objectives carried out under the direction of a BME faculty member and a willing sponsor at a field site, using resources not normally available on campus. Credit is based upon written and oral presentations demonstrating the achievement of the objectives of the course. Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BME
title: Group Tutorial
desc: A program of study arranged between a group of students and a faculty member. Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BME
title: Group Tutorial
desc: A program of independent study arranged between a group of students and a faculty member. Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BME
title: Senior Thesis Research
desc: Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BME
title: Senior Thesis or Research
desc: Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BME
title: Individual Study or Research
desc: Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BME
title: Individual Study or Research
desc: Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BME
title: Tutorial
desc: For fourth-year students majoring in bioinformatics or bioengineering.

subject: BME
title: Scientific Writing
desc: Covers effective writing styles for scientific communication for bio-science and engineering graduate students. Covers instruction for writing grant applications, scientific manuscripts, and thesis proposals. Students practice by preparing, editing, and evaluating each of these documents.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BME
title: Bioinformatics Models and Algorithms
desc: Covers bioinformatics models and algorithms: the use of computational techniques to convert the masses of information from biochemical experiments (DNA sequencing, DNA chips, and other high-throughput experimental methods) into useful information. Emphasis is on DNA and protein sequence alignment and analysis.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students. Undergraduates may enroll with prerequisite(s): BME 160 or CSE 20; and CSE 107 or STAT 131; and BME 105 or BIOL 105; and previous or concurrent enrollment in BIOC 100A or BME 101 or BIOL 100 or CHEM 103.

subject: BME
title: Applied Gene Technology
desc: Detailed insight into the techniques and technological trends in genomics and transcriptomics, building the necessary foundations for further research in genetic association studies, population genetic association studies, population genetics, diagnostics, medicine, and drug development. Students should already have a deeper understanding of the basic tools of molecular biotechnology than acquired in introductory courses in biotechnology, biochemistry, and molecular biotechnology.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BME
title: Mathematics of the Mind
desc: Investigates the mind as an adaptive system, the evolutionary history of the brain, and mathematical theories of knowledge representation and learning in humans and machines. Students build Jupyter notebooks that interact with human cerebral cortex organoids to explore adaptive processes in neural circuits. Taught in conjunction with BME 118. Students cannot receive credit for this course and BME 118.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students. Students should have knowledge of calculus, linear algebra, and Python programming.

subject: BME
title: Introduction to Basic Laboratory Techniques
desc: Laboratory course providing hands-on training in fundamental techniques used to express, isolate, and analyze genes in prokaryotic cells. Introduction to common laboratory instruments and fundamental skills required for basic research in molecular biology and biomolecular engineering.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): CHEM 1M or CHEM 3BL, or CHEM 4BL. Enrollment is restricted to bioengineering, bioinformatics, and biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics majors and proposed majors.

subject: BME
title: Protein Design and Engineering
desc: Explore computational protein design approaches and engineering techniques. Students learn to engineer functional proteins, formulate a protein design project, and communicate research effectively for practical applications. Taught in conjunction with BME 128. Students cannot receive credit for this course and BME 128.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BME
title: Protein and Cell Engineering
desc: Focuses on established and novel strategies for protein and cell engineering. Explores concepts, design, and practical applications of engineered proteins, cells, and organisms as research tools and in therapeutic applications. Recommended for graduate students with interests in bioengineering.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students. Undergraduates by permission of instructor.

subject: BME
title: Foundations of Design and Experimentation in Molecular Biology
desc: Project-based laboratory course providing hands-on training in fundamental molecular biology and biomolecular engineering techniques used to manipulate expression of DNA and proteins in prokaryotic cells. Students are introduced to essential processes in experimental design. (Formerly Foundations of Design and Experimentation in Molecular Biology, Part I.)
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 21L. Enrollment is restricted to bioengineering, bioinformatics, and biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics majors and proposed majors.

subject: BME
title: Introduction to Computational Genomics and Systems Biology
desc: Introductory and intermediate-level topics in computational genomics, DNA and RNA sequence analysis, mapping, quantification, detection of variants and their associations with disease. Covers topics in machine-learning, probabilistic graphical models, gene regulatory network inference, and single cell analysis. Students conduct related independent research.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 205. Enrollment is restricted to juniors, seniors, and graduate students.

subject: BME
title: Advanced Computational Genomics and Systems Biology
desc: Covers advanced topics in computational genomics, DNA and RNA sequence analysis, mapping, quantification, detection of variants and their associations with disease. Topics include machine-learning, probabilistic graphical models, gene regulatory network inference, and single cell analysis. Students participate in teams in a computational analysis competition.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 230A. Enrollment is restricted to juniors, seniors, and graduate students.

subject: BME
title: Evolutionary Genomics
desc: Covers major recent advances in evolutionary genomics. Students learn to analyze and interpret scientific writing in depth. Students also present on work covered in the class and produce one research or review paper. Students may not receive credit for this course and course 132.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students. BME 105 or BIOL 105 or equivalent courses in higher-level genetic processes are highly recommended.

subject: BME
title: Applied RNA Bioinformatics
desc: Teaches methods for RNA gene discovery; gene expression quantification; probabalistic modeling, secondary structure/trans-interaction prediction; mRNA splicing; and functional analysis. Emphasis on leveraging comparative genomics and employing high-throughput RNA sequencing data. Includes lectures, scientific literature discussion, problem sets, and final gene-discovery project.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to seniors and graduate students.

subject: BME
title: Foundations of Design and Experimentation in Molecular Biology, Part II
desc: Laboratory-based course extending the wet lab skills developed in the first two quarters of the BME 2x series with bioinformatics skills that form the foundation of biomolecular engineering. Focuses on sequencing of low-diversity environmental samples, including: field sampling, DNA extraction from those samples, library preparation, hands-on sequencing using a Nanopore device, base-calling of the raw data, assembly of contigs, quality assessment, contig assignment to species/bins, automated annotation of a single assemblage from collection genome publication.
prereq_raw: Prerequisites: BME 22L. Enrollment is restricted to bioengineering, bioinformatics, and biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics majors and proposed majors.

subject: BME
title: Applied Visualization and Analysis of Scientific Data
desc: Python and its Numpy, Scipy, and Matplotlib packages as well as Inkscape are used to generate publication quality figures from scientific data. Students cannot receive credit for this course and course 163.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 160 or BME 205. Prerequisite(s) can be waived in cases where students have required programming skills. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BME
title: Precision Medicine
desc: Focuses on modern "precision" approaches to understanding human health, where every patient is unique. Explores basic and clinical discoveries and 'omics-based medicine for the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of disease. Emphasis is on genomic approaches and applications to cancer.
prereq_raw: Enrollment restricted to juniors, seniors, and graduate students.

subject: BME
title: Stem Cell Epi/Genomics
desc: Course focuses on the application of epi/genomic technologies of stem cells. Topics include 'omics to interrogate pluripotency, cell lineages, hierarchies, trajectories, epigenomic reprogramming. Class includes hands-on computational analysis of epi/genomics data. For graduate/postdoctoral trainees engaged in stem cell research. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students and by permission of the instructor. Basic programming knowledge is recommended.

subject: BME
title: Entrepreneurship in Biotechnology
desc: Focuses on contemporary issues in commercializing biotechnology and genomics, emphasizing development of teamwork and communication skills. Topics include intellectual property management, fundraising, market analysis, and technology development as related to biotechnology start-ups. Students perform real-world tasks preparing for commercialization. Taught in conjunction with Biomolecular Engineering 175.

subject: BME
title: Stem Cell Biology
desc: Basic stem cell concepts, experimental approaches, and therapeutic potential are discussed. Students gain experience in reading and critically evaluating the primary scientific literature. Students cannot receive credit for this course and BME 178.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students in PBSE program (Program in Biomedical Science and Engineering: Biomolecular Engineering and Bioinformatics (BMEB), Microbial Biology and Pathogenesis (MICRO), Chemical Biology, Biochemistry and Biophysics (CB3), Molecular, Cell and Developmental Biology (MCDB)) or consent of instructor.

subject: BME
title: Seminar on Bioinformatics and Bioengineering
desc: Weekly seminar series covering topics of current research in computational biology, and bioinformatics. Current research work and literature in these areas are discussed. Short papers reflecting on presentations required. Available for Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory (or Pass/No Pass) grading only.

subject: BME
title: Seminar on Processive Enzymes and Nanopores
desc: Weekly seminar series covering experimental research in nanopore technology and single-molecule analysis of polymerase function. Current research work and literature is discussed. Students lead some discussions and participate in all meetings.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students. Qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BME
title: Seminar in Cancer Genomics
desc: Presents current computational biology research to identify genomics-based signatures of cancer onset, progression, and treatment response. Examples of such investigations include: genetic pathway interpretation of multivariate high-throughput datasets; discovery of mutations in whole-genome sequence; identifications and quantification of gene isoforms, alleles, and copy number variants; and machine-learning tools to predict clinical outcomes. Students present their own research, host journal clubs, and attend lectures and teleconferences to learn about research conducted by national and international projects.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BME
title: Seminar on Protein Engineering
desc: Weekly seminar series covering experimental research in protein structure, function, and engineering. Current research work and literature in this area are discussed. Students lead some discussions and participate in all meetings.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BME
title: Seminar in Genomics
desc: Current topics in genomics including high-throughput sequencing, genome assembly, and comparative genomics. Students design and implement independent research projects. Weekly laboratory meetings are held to discuss these projects and related research in the field.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students

subject: BME
title: Blood Cell Development
desc: Weekly seminar covering topics in current research on blood cell development and stem cell biology. Current research and literature in these areas discussed. Students lead some discussions and participate in all meetings.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students. Undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BME
title: Seminar on Cell Fate Decisions
desc: Weekly seminar series covering experimental research in cell fate decisions. Current research work and literature in this area is discussed. Students lead some discussions and participate in all meetings. Available for Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory or Pass/No Pass grading only.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students only; qualified undergraduate students may enroll with permission of the instructor.

subject: BME
title: Live Cell Biotechnology Seminar
desc: Weekly seminar series covering topics of current computational and experimental research in live cell biotechnology. Current research work and literature in this area are discussed. Students lead some discussions and participate in all meetings. (Formerly offered as Seminar in Comparative Genomics.)
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BME
title: Seminar in Computational Genomics and Biomedicine
desc: Research seminar of the UCSC Computational Genomic Laboratory and Platform Teams. Students receive hands-on instruction in modern computational methods to address research questions. Topics include: genomic and transcriptomic sequence analysis methods, comparative and evolutionary genomics, big-data genomic analysis, biomedical data sharing, and precision medicine. Students attend and participate in monthly lab meetings, monthly all-hands meetings, where students give a quick report on their progress and the next month's goals, and a bi-weekly journal club, where pairs of students present and discuss a paper of their choosing with the lab. Students also participate in hands-on, active computational laboratory-based research. Student evaluation is based on suitable progress toward research goals and graduate program progress.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BME
title: Seminar in Computational Genetics
desc: Weekly seminar series covering topics and experimental research in computational genetics. Current research work and literature in this area discussed. Students lead some discussions and participate in all meetings.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BME
title: Seminar on Chromosome Biology and Function
desc: Weekly seminar series covering experimental research in chromosome structure and repeat biology. Current research work and literature in this area is discussed. Students lead some discussions and participate in all meetings. Available for Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory or Pass/No Pass grading only.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students. Qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BME
title: Seminar in Transcriptomics
desc: Covers current topics in computational and experimental research in transcriptomics. Current research work and literature discussed. Weekly laboratory meetings held to discuss these projects and related research in the field.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BME
title: Seminar on Nanotechnology and Biosensors
desc: Weekly seminar covering topics of research in the development of new tools and technologies to detect and study genes and proteins. Latest research work and literature in these areas are discussed. Students lead some discussions and participate in all meetings.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BME
title: Seminar in Stem Cell Genomics
desc: Weekly seminar series covering topics in research on stem cell genomics. Current research and literature in this area is discussed. Students lead some discussions and participate in all meetings.
prereq_raw: Enrollment restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with instructor permission.

subject: BME
title: Seminar in Computational Functional Genomics
desc: Weekly seminar series covering topics of current computational and experimental research in computational functional genomics. Current research work and literature in this area discussed. Students lead some discussions and participate in all meetings.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BME
title: Seminar in Neuroengineering and Systems Neuroscience
desc: Discusses research topics in 3D stem cell-derived brain organoid models, neuroengineering and systems neuroscience. Students lead some discussions and participate in all meetings. Available for Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory or Pass/No Pass grading only. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduate students may enroll with permission of the instructor.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BME
title: Immunogenomics Seminar
desc: Journal club and research presentations in immunogenomics. Enrollment is by consent of the instructor and is restricted to graduate students, juniors, and seniors.

subject: BME
title: Microbial Symbiosis
desc: Seminar course consisting of the Russell Lab's weekly meeting to cover lab business, present and discuss new results, practice presentations, and read recent scientific literature. May be repeated for credit. Enrollment is restricted to graduate students and is by permission of the instructor.

subject: BME
title: Seminar on Protein Design
desc: Includes the Yeh Lab’s weekly group meeting to discuss new data, present research paper, pitch new scientific idea, cover lab business, and practice presentations. Available for Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory or Pass/No Pass grading only.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students only; qualified undergraduate students may enroll with permission of the instructor.

subject: BME
title: Seminar in Population and Evolutionary Genomics
desc: Covers major recent topics in evolutionary and population genomics. Consists primarily of discussions of recent literature and updates on group members' research. Enrollment is available only to members of the Corbett-Detig laboratory.

subject: BME
title: Bioethics in the 21st Century: Science, Business, and Society
desc: Serves science and non-science majors interested in bioethics. Guest speakers and instructors lead discussions of major ethical questions having arisen from research in genetics, medicine, and industries supported by this knowledge. Students may not receive credit for both this course and BME 80G /PHIL 80G.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students.

subject: BME
title: Seminar in Biomolecular Engineering
desc: Weekly seminar series covering topics of bioinformatics and biomolecular engineering research. Current research work and literature in this area discussed. Students lead some discussions and participate in all meetings.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to graduate students; qualified undergraduates may enroll with permission of instructor.

subject: BME
title: Research in Bioinformatics
desc: Independent research in bioinformatics under faculty supervision. Although this course may be repeated for credit, not every degree program accepts a repeated course toward degree requirements. Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BME
title: Independent Study or Research
desc: Independent study or research under faculty supervision. Although course may be repeated for credit, not every degree program accepts a repeated course toward degree requirements. Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.

subject: BME
title: Strategies for a Successful Summer Internship
desc: BME 35 is a companion course for UCSC students in the QB3 Summer Internship Program. BME 35 and the associated internship provide hands-on experience working in a lab on campus or at an industry partner. The course and internship are designed to provide an intensive research experience augmenting their major and prior coursework.

subject: BME
title: Introduction to Biotechnology
desc: Introduces the tools and applications of biotechnology in the fields of medicine, agriculture, the environment, and industry.

subject: BME
title: Applied Electronics for Bioengineers Part 1
desc: Lab-based course that introduces measuring, modeling, and designing electronics circuits, emphasizing voltage dividers and complex impedance culminating in simple, negative-feedback op amp circuits for amplifying audio signals.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): MATH 19A; or MATH 11A by consent of instructor. High school physics recommended. Enrollment is restricted to bioengineering and biomolecular engineering & bioinformatics majors and proposed majors; other majors by consent.

subject: BME
title: Applied Electronics for Bioengineers Part 2
desc: Lab-based course that introduces designing, measuring, and modeling electronics circuits, emphasizing RC filters and negative-feedback amplifiers for various sensors circuits for amplifying audio signals, design of multi-stage amplifiers, instrumentation amplifiers, and class-D power amplifiers.
prereq_raw: Prerequisite(s): BME 51A.

subject: BME
title: Introduction to Lab Groups
desc: Course intended to assist second-year biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics undergraduates find research labs that they might join. Students sit in on different lab group meetings, read papers recommended by the lab groups, and report back to other students in the class both verbally and in writing. Course is offered for pass/no pass only.
prereq_raw: Enrollment is restricted to sophomore and junior proposed biomolecular engineering and bioinformatics majors, or by permission of the instructor.

subject: BME
title: Bioethics in the 21st Century: Science, Business, and Society
desc: Serves science and non-science majors interested in bioethics. Guest speakers and instructors lead discussions of major ethical questions having arisen from research in genetics, medicine, and industries supported by this knowledge.

subject: BME
title: The Human Genome
desc: Course will focus on understanding human genes. Accessible to non-science majors. Will cover principles of human inheritance and techniques used in gene analysis. The evolutionary, social, ethical, and legal issues associated with knowledge of the human genome will be discussed.

subject: BME
title: Group Tutorial
desc: Provides a means for a small group of students to study a particular topic in consultation with a faculty sponsor. Students submit petition to sponsoring agency.
